records.current_localsOnly: The 2023 legal-gender-recognition and gender-affirming-care bans are resident-facing; the extremism-designation machinery (convictions, NGO liquidation) targets resident organisations and individuals.
records.current_outOfScope: Advisory-level risks are trans-unrelated: the ongoing war, wrongful-detention risk, and arbitrary law enforcement affect any traveller regardless of LGBT status.

sources.claim: UK Home Office country policy and information note, Russia, SOGI (June 2025; assessment updated 11 June 2025): establishes the national baseline this region is scored against - same-sex activity is not criminalised, but same-sex marriage and gender transition are banned with no specific legal protections. The 'gay propaganda' law carries administrative fines with repeat offences punishable by up to 4 years in prison; the International LGBT Movement extremism designation carries 2-6 years for participating and 6-10 for organising. Between 2022 and 2024 at least 139 people in Russia were impacted by anti-LGBT+ laws (convictions, detentions, extremism prosecutions). No Far Eastern Federal District-specific findings appear in the note; the record's stated no-deviation, national-score assessment rests on this baseline.

Human Rights Watch (30 June 2025): Russian courts have issued 101 convictions for 'extremism' tied to the International LGBT Movement following the 2023 Supreme Court extremist designation. Between January 2024 and June 2025 at least 20 people faced criminal charges (one died by suicide in pretrial detention; courts sentenced two to prison), and 81 people in 98 cases were found guilty under article 20.3 of the Code of Administrative Offenses for displaying banned symbols; participants face up to 12 years in prison.
